officialLinks.label: How do I calculate my GPA?

helpIntro: Stanford uses a 4.3 scale: each letter grade is worth a fixed number of grade points per unit. Your GPA is total grade points divided by GPA-bearing units.
helpNote: Coterminal students should calculate undergraduate and graduate records separately.
helpExample: 5-unit A+ = 5 × 4.3 = 21.5 points. Sum all course points, divide by total GPA-bearing units, and round to three decimals.

gradeExplanations.L: Temporary grade (Pass, grade to follow). Counts as 2.0 points until the final grade replaces it.
gradeExplanations.NP: No Pass. Units count in GPA at 0.0 points.
gradeExplanations.NC: No Credit. Excluded from GPA — units and points do not count.

specialTypes.name: GSB course
specialTypes.note: GSB courses use their own grading system (H 4.14, HP 3.54, P 3.24, LP 2.94, U 0.00). For undergraduate and non-MBA/MSx graduate records, these grades count toward your general University GPA. MBA and MSx students should consult the GSB Registrar.

specialTypes.name: External transfer course
specialTypes.note: External transfer courses are excluded from the Stanford GPA calculation. Check with the Registrar about transfer credit policies.

repeatPolicy.note: Stanford typically retains both the original and repeated course on the transcript; grade points are replaced according to university policy. Confirm with the Registrar for your specific situation.
